title: Roadmap to AI Governance for Financial Services — Q3 2026 Edition

citations.claim: The EU AI Act classifies AI systems used for creditworthiness assessment of natural persons as high-risk, imposing risk-management, data-governance, logging and human-oversight obligations on financial-services deployers.
citations.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

citations.claim: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) organises trustworthy-AI practice into four functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — that financial institutions adapt as the backbone of an AI governance programme.
citations.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

citations.claim: The UK PRA and FCA supervisory approach treats AI and machine-learning model risk within existing model-risk-management and senior-management-accountability expectations, requiring firms to evidence governance, validation and ongoing monitoring.
citations.publisher: Bank of England — Prudential Regulation Authority
